Now the U.S. is in there, and they're worried that we'll have more generous credits and so forth with the Russians than they do.

They don't want a confrontation with the U.S., and that's on their minds.
On the trade bill, for example, while they're quite apprehensive about some aspects of it,
they're clearly happier to have a trade bill and to have the U.S. in there in negotiations
than for us to throw up our hands and not have one, which they would regard as kind of a withdrawal.
And I think it also seemed to me that they looked for U.S. initiatives in the military and the trade area.
And I was amazed at how easy it was to do what we did.
That is, basically, in the first Paris conference, they were collaborating on it.
And we kind of stopped and said, now, look, we're not going to answer the things that you want until you've thought through better.
